source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Using the Parkland formula, a 60-kg adult with 50% TBSA burns needs how much LR in the first 8 hours?
questions.rationale: 4 × 60 × 50 = 12,000 mL/24 h; half (6,000 mL) in the first 8 hours from time of injury.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Parkland Formula (PDF p. 410)
questions.quote: Day 1: Half to be given in first 8 hours

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Burn fluid replacement time is calculated from:
questions.rationale: Formulas are calculated from the time of injury.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fluid Resuscitation (PDF p. 409)
questions.quote: calculated from the time of injury and not from the time of arrival

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is the most sensitive indicator of adequate burn fluid resuscitation?
questions.rationale: Urine output of 30–50 mL/h reflects cardiac output and perfusion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fluid Resuscitation (PDF p. 409)
questions.quote: Urinary output is the most sensitive assessment parameter

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During the acute (diuretic) burn phase, the nurse expects:
questions.rationale: Fluid returns to vessels; K shifts into cells; hematocrit falls.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Phase (PDF p. 409)
questions.quote: Hypokalemia (K+ shifts back into the cells)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why are IM injections avoided for burn pain in the emergent phase?
questions.rationale: Hypovolemia and fluid shifts make IM/SC absorption unreliable; give IV opioids.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Burn Pain Management (PDF p. 410)
questions.quote: Avoid IM or SC routes because absorption through the soft tissue is unreliable

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When should analgesics be given before burn wound care?
questions.rationale: Premedicate about 30 minutes before painful procedures.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Burn Pain Management (PDF p. 410)
questions.quote: Medicate client 30 minutes prior to painful procedures

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which diet supports burn wound healing?
questions.rationale: Hypermetabolism requires high protein, calories, vitamins, and minerals.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Burn Nutrition (PDF p. 410)
questions.quote: High in protein

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Hydrotherapy for burns is limited to 30 minutes or less to prevent:
questions.rationale: Prolonged immersion increases heat and sodium loss through the wound.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hydrotherapy (PDF p. 411)
questions.quote: done for 30 minutes or less

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should a circumferential burn dressing be applied?
questions.rationale: Wrap distally to proximally; fingers and toes individually.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Wound Dressing (PDF p. 411)
questions.quote: Distally to proximally

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A circumferential arm burn causes weak distal pulses. Which procedure relieves constriction?
questions.rationale: Escharotomy incises the eschar lengthwise to restore circulation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Escharotomy (PDF p. 411)
questions.quote: A lengthwise incision is made through the burn eschar to relieve constriction

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on silver sulfadiazine has a WBC drop on day 2. The nurse knows:
questions.rationale: Transient leukopenia may occur and resolves in 2–3 days.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Topical Antimicrobials (PDF p. 412)
questions.quote: May cause transient leukopenia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which topical burn agent penetrates eschar and may cause metabolic acidosis?
questions.rationale: Mafenide penetrates eschar, is painful, and may cause metabolic acidosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Topical Antimicrobials (PDF p. 412)
questions.quote: May cause metabolic acidosis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Silver nitrate dressings require monitoring of:
questions.rationale: Silver nitrate draws electrolytes out; keep dressings wet and monitor Na and K.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Topical Antimicrobials (PDF p. 412)
questions.quote: Monitor serum sodium (Na+) and potassium (K+).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which graft provides permanent burn wound coverage?
questions.rationale: Autograft uses the client's own skin; others are temporary.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Wound Closure (PDF p. 412)
questions.quote: Permanent wound coverage.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pig skin used as a temporary burn covering is a:
questions.rationale: Xenograft (heterograft) is porcine; allograft is cadaver skin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Wound Closure (PDF p. 413)
questions.quote: Porcine (pig) skin is harvested after slaughter and preserved.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why are young children at greater risk from burns than adults?
questions.rationale: Thinner skin burns deeper; higher fluid proportion raises fluid and heat loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, The Burned Child (PDF p. 413)
questions.quote: a more severe burn in a child than an adult because a child’s skin is thinner

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Neurons that carry impulses from receptors to the CNS are:
questions.rationale: Afferent neurons carry sensory input to the CNS.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Neurons (PDF p. 414)
questions.quote: transmit impulses from receptors to the CNS

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Broca's area, controlling motor speech, is in the:
questions.rationale: Broca's (frontal) is expressive speech; Wernicke's (temporal) is comprehension.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cerebrum (PDF p. 414)
questions.quote: Contains Broca’s area (motor control of speech)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client cannot understand spoken language after a stroke. Which area is affected?
questions.rationale: Wernicke's area in the temporal lobe controls language comprehension.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cerebrum (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: Wernicke’s area: language comprehension

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which brain structure controls balance and coordination?
questions.rationale: Cerebellum controls fine movement, balance, and proprioception.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cerebellum (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: Controls fine movement, balance, and position or proprioception.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The cardiac, respiratory, and vasomotor centers are located in the:
questions.rationale: The medulla contains vital centers and reflexes such as coughing and vomiting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Medulla (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: Contains cardiac centers, respiratory centers, vasomotor centers

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which brain structure regulates body temperature?
questions.rationale: Hypothalamus regulates temperature, food and fluid intake, and autonomic function.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothalamus (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: Regulation of body temperature

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Testing the corneal reflex assesses which cranial nerve?
questions.rationale: Trigeminal nerve: facial sensation, corneal reflex, mastication.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerves (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: Facial sensation, corneal reflex, mastication

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Asking the client to shrug the shoulders tests cranial nerve:
questions.rationale: CN XI innervates sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerves (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How many pairs of spinal nerves are there?
questions.rationale: 31 pairs: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Spinal Nerves (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: Composed of 31 pairs
